title: Land decking bundles across three joists, within a foot of the bearing end
instruction: Land the two yellow decking bundles as OSHA 1926.757(e)(4) and (e)(5) require: one flat across the left three grey joists and one across the right three, each square to the joists with its long edge within 40 mm (1 ft at this scale) of a red girder, never at mid-span and never stacked. The blue mat between the arms is the handover spot.
context: On steel erection jobs, decking bundles are often landed on joists before all bridging is installed. OSHA 1926.757 allows that only if, among other conditions, the joists are attached at both ends and at least one row of bridging is installed and anchored ((e)(4)(iii)-(iv)), the bundle lies across at least three joists ((e)(4)(ii)), and its edge is within 1 ft of the bearing surface ((e)(5)), because a mid-span load can buckle joists not yet fully bridged. The natural centred, mid-span landing is the one the rule forbids. The bundles lie out of the right arm's reach, so one is passed across on the mat. Done by: construction laborers, ironworkers (signalling and guiding the landing).
setup: A scale model of a steel-framed floor bay, 1 ft = 40 mm (1:7.6), all of it fixed (clamped or screwed to the table) except the two bundles. Six grey-painted steel box sections, stand-ins for open-web steel joists, each 20 mm wide, 50 mm tall and 300 mm long, run straight away from the arms from 23 to 53 cm in front of the arm bases, 80 mm apart on centre (2 ft): their centres are 4, 12 and 20 cm left and 4, 12 and 20 cm right of the centre line between the arm bases (the arm bases are 61 cm apart). Their ends butt against two dark red painted steel box sections, stand-ins for girders, each 20 mm thick, 520 mm long side to side (centred on the centre line) and 70 mm tall, so their tops stand 20 mm above the joist tops: the front girder from 21 to 23 cm in front of the arm bases, the back girder from 53 to 55 cm. A blue rubber mat, 70 mm front to back, 260 mm side to side and 4 mm thick, is taped down on the centre line, its centre 13 cm in front of the arm bases: the handover spot. Two identical yellow-painted solid wood blocks, stand-ins for bundles of steel deck sheets, each 220 mm long, 60 mm wide and 40 mm tall (5.5 x 1.5 x 1 ft at scale), 0.4 kg, lie flat on the bare table to the left of the bay with their long sides running left to right, centred 40 cm left of the centre line (9.5 cm outboard of the left arm's base), one 19 cm and one 30 cm in front of the arm bases; a tape outline marks each start. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Each half of the bay is worth 0.5: the left half is joists 1 to 3 (the three left of the centre line), the right half joists 4 to 6. Each bundle counts for at most one half; the bundles are identical, so either may land on either half, and the pairing of bundles to halves that scores more is used. A bundle earns 0.5 x S x D for its half, and nothing unless all of these hold: it is still (moving under 1 cm/s and turning under 0.5 rad/s); its lowest point is from 3 mm below to 0.5 mm above the joist tops (50 mm above the table), so not on a girder, the table, the mat or the other bundle, and not held above them; its outline lies between the two girder faces (within 2 mm); it is tilted at most 3 degrees, either big face up; its long side is within 15 degrees of square to the joists. S counts that half's joists that have at least 15 mm of their 20 mm top width under the bundle's centre line (the 220 mm line along its length through its centre), measured across the joist, and that the bundle sits down on: where each of the bundle's two long bottom edges crosses that joist's centre line, its bottom is from 3 mm below to 0.5 mm above the joist's top (so a bundle still held with one end or one long edge raised gets no count for the joists it hangs over). All 3 S = 1, exactly 2 S = 0.5, 1 or none S = 0; joists of the other half don't count. D depends on the gap g from the nearer girder face to the bundle's long edge on that side, measured at the end of that edge farther from the girder: g of 40 mm or less D = 1; between 40 and 70 mm D = (70 - g) / 30, falling linearly; 70 mm or more D = 0 (a square bundle's centre is then 100 mm from the girder face, the edge of the mid-span band). Both girders are bearing ends. Both halves in full: 1.0. The score is 0 overall if a bundle lies on the joists (lowest point from 3 mm below to 0.5 mm above their tops, over a joist) with its centre 100 mm or more from both girder faces, however it is turned (the middle 100 mm of the span, 33 to 43 cm in front of the arm bases), or with any part of its outline seen from above reaching the middle of the span (38 cm in front of the arm bases), or if one bundle rests on the other (its bottom from 5 mm below to 0.5 mm above the other's top, their outlines seen from above overlapping by more than 2 mm). A bundle left on the mat, on the table or on the floor earns nothing. The trial ends at 1.0 once both halves score in full and both bundles have stayed still for 2.5 s; otherwise the score at the last step counts.
reset_notes: Lay both bundles back flat on their tape outlines left of the bay, long sides running left to right. The joists, girders and mat are fixed and stay in place; check the mat's tape before each trial.
fidelity: Approximate: the joists and girders are solid fixed boxes, the joists butted against the girder faces instead of bearing on seats, and nothing bends or buckles; a mid-span or stacked landing stands in for the collapse. A bundle of deck sheets is one rigid block, and landing is by hand rather than crane. Every object has the same rubber-like friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic), grippier than painted steel.
